before.title: 'Anti-Pollution Fault' Warning — Emissions System Faults
before.description: A very common 206 complaint on multiplexed cars is the 'Anti-pollution fault' message on the multifunction display, often accompanied by the engine management light, misfire, lost power or limp mode. It is a generic emissions-system alert triggered by a range of root causes documented across owner forums: failing ignition coils, lambda (oxygen) sensor faults, sticking EGR valves, sticky hydraulic tappets and, on neglected cars, catalytic converters damaged by sustained misfiring. Because the message is generic, owners frequently replace the wrong parts before reading the stored fault codes.
before.solution: Read the stored DTCs with PSA-capable diagnostics rather than guessing; the accepted fixes are replacing the specific failed component — most commonly an ignition coil pack or lambda sensor, cleaning or replacing the EGR valve, or replacing a misfire-damaged catalytic converter in advanced cases.
symptoms: 'Anti-pollution fault' message on the multifunction display
Engine management light on
Misfire or juddering, especially under load
Loss of power or limp mode
Engine cutting out shortly after the warning appears

proposal.title: 'Anti-Pollution Fault' Warning — Emissions System Faults

proposal.solution: Record the exact warning, DTC status and freeze-frame data, then test ignition, fueling, air metering, exhaust sensors, EGR operation and catalyst efficiency as separate paths under engine/VIN-specific service information. Avoid continued driving with a severe misfire because unburned fuel can overheat the catalyst. Do not buy a coil pack, oxygen sensor, EGR valve or catalyst from this page; the failed path and fitment must be established first.

before.title: BSI (Built-in Systems Interface) Body Control Unit Faults
before.description: The 206's BSI body control computer, which governs central locking, wipers, lights, instrument functions and the immobiliser, is prone to corrupted software, dry solder joints and water ingress — water entering through the bonnet vent and poorly drained plenum chamber can drip onto the unit and fuse box. A glitched or failed BSI causes seemingly random electrical chaos: wipers and lights operating on their own, dead central locking, erratic dashboard readings, and immobiliser faults that leave the car unable to start. Owner clubs maintain a well-known battery-disconnect 'BSI reset' procedure because the fault is so widespread on multiplexed (mid-2001-on) cars.
before.solution: First attempt the documented BSI reset (controlled battery disconnect/reboot sequence); persistent faults require repair of the unit's solder joints by a specialist or a replacement BSI that must be coded/cloned to the car. Address water ingress at the bonnet vent and plenum drains to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Car will not start with immobiliser/anti-theft fault shown
Central locking stops working or operates by itself
Wipers or headlights switch on without input
Erratic instrument cluster readings and warning lights
Electric windows and rear wiper dead simultaneously

before.title: COM2000 Indicator/Wiper Stalk Unit Failure
before.description: The COM2000 steering-column module — which combines the indicator and wiper stalks, horn contact and the multiplex electronics behind them — is a notorious 206 weak point, particularly on multiplexed cars built from July 2001. Worn or grease-fouled contacts cause indicators to self-trigger, cancel erratically or only work with the lights on, headlights to flash when indicating, and the horn to stop working. The fault was so widespread that Honest John records Peugeot offering a free fix in France from December 2002 and in the UK from January 2003 for cars under warranty.
before.solution: Replace the COM2000 unit (roughly £130-£180 for the part depending on trim, plus fitting behind the steering wheel); confident DIYers sometimes succeed in cleaning and re-greasing the internal contacts, but unit replacement is the accepted lasting fix.
symptoms: Indicators come on or cancel by themselves
Indicators only work with headlights switched on
Main beam flashes when using the indicator stalk
Horn stops working
Wiper functions behave erratically

before.title: Fuel Gauge Sender Unit Failure
before.description: The in-tank fuel level sender on the 206 commonly fails or misreads: the float arm sticks at certain levels, the resistive track wears, or the connector terminals on top of the pump/sender module corrode and lose contact. Owners see the gauge stuck on full or empty, wild fluctuation between readings, or a permanently lit low-fuel light, making it easy to run out of fuel unexpectedly. The fault is well documented across 206 owner forums with established access and repair procedures.
before.solution: Access the sender through the hatch under the rear seat cushion, clean and re-tension the connector terminals and inspect the wiring; if the float or resistive track is worn, replace the sender (or combined pump/sender) unit. No tank removal is required.
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck on full or empty
Gauge fluctuates wildly between readings
Low fuel warning light on with a full tank
Gauge reading changes after hitting bumps
Running out of fuel despite gauge showing remaining range

before.title: Head Gasket Failure
before.description: The TU-series engines in the 206 are prone to head gasket failure, particularly when the cooling system is neglected. Overheating episodes accelerate gasket deterioration, leading to coolant-oil mixing and white exhaust smoke.
before.solution: Replace the head gasket, machine the cylinder head surface if warped, and flush the cooling system. Inspect and replace the thermostat and water pump preventatively.
symptoms: White exhaust smoke
Coolant loss without visible leak
Oil-coolant emulsion on dipstick
Overheating

before.title: Ignition Coil Pack Failure (Petrol TU Engines)
before.description: The wasted-spark coil pack on the 206's small petrol engines (1.1 KFV, 1.4 KFW and related TU units) is a frequent failure item: one of the two internal coils breaks down, dropping spark on a paired set of cylinders (1/4 or 2/3). Owners report intermittent misfire, rough running, the engine cutting out and refusing to restart until it cools, and the management light flickering. Forum consensus also warns that cheap aftermarket replacement packs often fail repeatedly or seat poorly, causing the fault to return.
before.solution: Replace the coil pack — OEM-quality (Sagem/Valeo/Bosch) units are strongly recommended over cheap aftermarket packs — along with spark plugs if worn. The job is a straightforward DIY or sub-one-hour shop task on these engines.
symptoms: Misfire on two cylinders, rough idle
Intermittent stalling or cutting out, restarts after cooling
Engine management light flickering or on
Hesitation and loss of power under acceleration
Hard or failed starting in damp weather

before.title: Rear Axle Torsion Beam Trailing Arm Bearing Wear
before.description: The 206's rear torsion-beam axle uses needle roller bearings on the trailing arm shafts that are poorly sealed against the elements; water ingress rusts the bearings away, and the failed rollers then chew up the arm shaft and the inside of the axle tube. The result is the classic PSA rear-end failure: knocking over bumps, visible negative camber on the rear wheels, wheel wobble and rapid inner-edge tyre wear. Left unattended, severe play degrades handling and the axle tube itself is destroyed, making a simple bearing kit repair impossible.
before.solution: If caught early, fit a trailing arm bearing and shaft repair kit; once the axle tube bearing surfaces are scored, the accepted fix is a fully reconditioned exchange rear axle from a specialist, followed by rear geometry/ride-height check. Repairing a seized, rusted original axle DIY is generally considered impractical.
symptoms: Knocking, clicking or squeaking from the rear over bumps
Rear wheels leaning in at the top (negative camber)
Rear wheel wobble visible when following the car
Excessive play when rocking the rear wheel
Rapid wear on the inner edges of the rear tyres
Rear ride height lower on one side
